Soap molecules have a hydrophilic head and a hydrophobic tail. The hydrophobic tails attach to grease, while the hydrophilic heads face water. This forms micelles that trap grease inside, allowing it to be rinsed away. Soap thus emulsifies grease, making it soluble in water.

Soap molecules have a hydrophilic head and a hydrophobic tail. The tail attaches to grease while the head stays in water. This forms micelles that trap grease inside. Rinsing washes away the micelles, removing the grease.
